summary: Lane 3 (deep enrichment) verified on the wire today, 2026-07-23. Headline: the enrichment fields split cleanly into three buckets — (a) cheaply and legally fillable at national scale from bulk open data, (b) fillable only at low yield via robots-respecting fetches of the shop's own site, (c) permanently NULL because no free legal US source exists. Bucket (a) is bigger than the repo currently exploits: I measured Overture 2026-07-22.0 over a CONUS bbox and found 10,924 rows at categories.primary='truck_repair' with phone 99.2%, website 70.3%, EMAIL 60.4%, socials 82.1% — and the pipeline in scripts/businesses_pipeline.py projects neither `emails` nor `socials` into staging at all, so ~6,600 truck-repair emails and ~9,000 social handles are being discarded on every pull. FSQ OS Places (Apache-2.0, gated-free HF token) independently carries `email` at 41.0% on US 'Automotive Repair Shop' (measured on 2,145,747 US rows across 10 of 81 mirror shards), making it the only legal BULK email source I could find; there is no other. Overture's own taxonomy already contains roadside_assistance, emergency_roadside_service, mobile_dent_repair, trailer_repair, truck_repair and welders — so "roadside breakdown", "mobile service", "towing", "welding", "tyre repair" are derivable from a licence-clean category field rather than from scraping. Bucket (b) is grim and I measured it rather than guessing: I sampled 120 real US (PA) auto-repair shop websites from FSQ, fetched each robots.txt-first with a polite UA, and only 42% returned HTTP 200 (39% of the recorded URLs are simply dead); of those reachable, 47% carry any JSON-LD but only 16% expose `telephone`, 12% `openingHours`, 4% `email`, and 0% expose any makesOffer/hasOfferCatalog/serviceType — meaning "services offered" is never in JSON-LD on small shop sites. Exactly one of 51 reachable sites used @type AutoRepair. End-to-end that is roughly 3% hours coverage per shop from website extraction. OSM is close to useless here at US scale: Overpass over a CONUS bbox gives shop=car_repair=52,713 with opening_hours on only 8,165 (15.5%), email on 1,042 (2.0%), service:vehicle:truck_repair on 448 (0.85%) and hgv=yes on 3 rows; shop=truck_repair is 330 nationally. Global taginfo confirms the tag family is tiny (shop=truck_repair 813, service:vehicle:truck_repair 1,381 worldwide). On franchise locators I was strict and the answer is mostly NO: Love's, Ryder and TA/Petro all carry explicit anti-scraping clauses in their Terms of Use, which I quoted verbatim from the live pages — those three are UNUSABLE regardless of their permissive robots.txt or their published location sitemaps. The truck OEMs (Freightliner, Peterbilt, Mack, Volvo, Western Star) serve allow-all robots.txt and Freightliner's dealer pages do carry schema.org LocalBusiness JSON-LD with telephone, but I could not retrieve their Terms of Use text (SPA-rendered or 404), so I am marking them UNVERIFIED rather than green-lighting them. Kenworth returns 403. The good news is that "Truck Brands Supported" is partially answerable without touching any locator: Overture's own `brand` field on truck-ish categories already resolves Penske (1,553), Ryder (431), Rush Truck Centers (107), TA-Petro (104), MHC Kenworth (62), TLG Peterbilt (22), Premier Truck Group (25), Velocity Truck Centers (23), Vanguard, TEC Equipment, TruckPro, FleetPride, Boss Truck Shop — and the Name Suggestion Index (BSD-3-Clause, 49,943 items, 17 under shop/truck_repair) normalises those names for free. Bucket (c): average rating, review count, review summary, photos and WhatsApp number have NO free legal US source and should be dropped from the schema rather than left as perpetually-NULL columns. On vocabulary, "District" must become County (free via Census TIGER county shapefile, public domain, or the keyless FCC Census Block API) and "PIN Code" must become 5-digit USPS ZIP (already present in Overture addresses[].postcode and FSQ postcode); note ZCTA is not ZIP. Finally the ODbL question: the OSMF Geocoding Guideline treats individual lookups as insubstantial but explicitly flags "a systematic attempt to aggregate all or substantially all Primary Features of a given type within a geographic area city-sized or larger" as substantial — which is precisely this enrichment task — while the Horizontal Map Layers Guideline says share-alike does not attach to a Feature Type whose data is entirely non-OSM. Together they confirm the repo's ruling section 3.1-4a is legally correct and, critically, mean that copying an OSM service:vehicle:* value into core.businesses as "services offered" would drag that whole feature type under ODbL share-alike. Keep OSM in osm.*, join at query time, expose it as a separately-attributed layer.

sources.why_it_matters: This is the single highest-leverage enrichment source and it is already wired into the repo — but under-exploited. MEASURED BY ME on release 2026-07-22.0, CONUS bbox: truck_repair n=10,924 → phone 99.2%, website 70.3%, email 60.4%, socials 82.1%, brand 5.2%, avg confidence 0.839. automotive_repair n=200,234 → phone 95.3%, website 67.4%, email 56.8%, socials 86.6%, brand 7.3%. towing_service n=21,825 → phone 99.7%, website 75.5%, email 49.2%. tire_dealer_and_repair n=42,647 → phone 98.0%, website 70.4%, email 57.9%, brand 29.8%. truck_dealer n=5,748 → phone 98.2%, website 87.1%, email 42.0%, brand 16.9%. I separately verified on one 4,595,262-row shard that Overture stores NULL and never an empty array for phones/emails/websites (0 empty arrays), so count(col) is a valid fill measure. CRITICAL GAP: scripts/businesses_pipeline.py's _OVERTURE_STAGING_COLS does not project `emails` or `socials`, and core.businesses has no column for either — roughly 6,600 truck_repair emails and ~9,000 social handles are discarded on every pull. Overture's brand field also directly answers 'Truck Brands Supported' for chains: on truck-ish categories the top brands are Penske 1553, Budget 376, Ryder System Inc 357, U-Haul 180, Enterprise 110, Rush Truck Centers 107, TravelCenters-TA-Petro 104, Ryder 74, RaceTrac 66, MHC Kenworth 62, Boss Truck Shop 43, FleetPride/GSFA 38, Premier Truck Group 25, Velocity Truck Centers 23, TLG Peterbilt 22, Find Trucks Service 22, Vanguard Truck Centers 21, W W Williams 20, Pilot 19, TEC Equipment 16, TruckPro LLC 14 — i.e. a large chunk of the OEM dealer network is recoverable with zero scraping.
sources.caveats: NO opening-hours field exists in the Overture places schema (confirmed on the live schema doc — operating_status is explicitly 'not an indication of opening hours'). No ratings, no reviews, no photos. The S3 bucket retains only one release at a time, so historical replay is impossible — observed_at must be the release date. Category quality is uneven: truck_stop has only 118 rows nationally while truck_gas_station has 2,660, so a single-category filter will badly under-count. Confidence is per-record and low-confidence junk exists (the repo's NYC-bbox pull produced exactly one truck_repair row, a Russian-language 'Вакансии' record at confidence 0.067).

sources.name: Overture Maps — categories taxonomy CSV
sources.why_it_matters: Confirms the legal, licence-clean basis for several requested service flags WITHOUT any scraping: roadside_assistance, emergency_roadside_service, mobile_dent_repair, trailer_repair, truck_repair, truck_repair_and_services_for_businesses, and welders all exist as Overture categories with full taxonomy paths under automotive > automotive_services_and_repair. So 'Roadside Breakdown', 'Mobile Service', 'Towing', 'Welding', 'Tyre Repair' can each be set from a category rather than inferred or scraped.
sources.caveats: A category is a coarse signal — it says a place IS a roadside-assistance business, not that a truck_repair shop also OFFERS roadside. Cross-service flags (a truck_repair shop that also does towing) are not expressible in a single-primary-category model; the honest render is NULL/unknown for those, never 'no'.

sources.approx_rows: unknown for the current HF release (latest release directory dt=2026-07-09); I measured the frozen mirror instead — see the source.coop row

That is a real, if mild, obligation Boss should be told about before a token is minted. Critically for this lane: FSQ's taxonomy has NO truck-specific repair category. I enumerated every US category label containing truck/diesel/fleet/trailer and got only 'Dining and Drinking > Food Truck', 'Community and Government > Trailer Park', and 'Travel and Transportation > Truck Stop'. Truck repair collapses into the generic 'Business and Professional Services > Automotive Service > Automotive Repair Shop'. FSQ also has NO hours, NO rating, NO review count.

sources.why_it_matters: This is the honest, measured verdict on OSM for this task, and it is negative. CONUS bbox, queried 2026-07-23: shop=car_repair = 52,713 total; with website 10,123 (19.2%); with opening_hours 8,165 (15.5%); with email 1,042 (2.0%); with service:vehicle:truck_repair 448 (0.85%); with hgv=yes THREE rows. shop=truck_repair nationally = 330. OSM cannot carry the enrichment load for US truck repair — it is a corroboration signal for a minority of rows, nothing more. Where it DOES win uniquely is opening_hours (the only free structured hours source that exists at all) and the 24/7 flag.
sources.caveats: ODbL share-alike is the binding constraint, not availability. Per the OSMF Geocoding Guideline, systematically aggregating all features of a type over a city-sized-or-larger area is 'substantial' — which is exactly this task — so OSM attribute values must NOT be copied into core.businesses. Also: my regex-combined phone query returned 0 due to my own Overpass escaping error, so the OSM phone fill rate for shop=car_repair in CONUS is UNMEASURED by me (global taginfo puts phone at 19.6% and contact:phone at 3.9% on shop=car_repair, which is the best available proxy). Be polite: I saw both 429 and 504 on heavy count queries; the free instance needs backoff.

And the fill rates on shop=car_repair globally: name 81.8%, phone 19.6%, opening_hours 17.3%, website 13.4%, brand 11.2%, email 3.9%, contact:email 1.9%, service:vehicle:car_repair 3.7%. opening_hours='24/7' is 738,170 uses = 15.7% of all opening_hours values, so the 24x7 flag is derivable by exact string match before you even need a parser.

sources.name: OSM wiki — Key:service:vehicle (tag semantics)
sources.why_it_matters: Confirms truck_repair, towing, tyres, batteries, electrical, transmission, glass, body_repair, diagnostics, inspection, oil_change, air_conditioning and brakes are all DOCUMENTED subkeys — so the vocabulary the task asked for exists and maps cleanly onto the requested service flags (welding is the notable absentee; use Overture's `welders` category instead).
sources.caveats: The wiki page does not state accepted VALUES (yes/no/only), which means a parser must treat any non-'no' value as present and must render absence as unknown, never as 'no'. There is NO OSM tag family for mobile/roadside truck service — I checked every key containing 'mobile' (top hits are communication:mobile_phone 256,973, snowmobile 118,675, mobile 70,749, contact:mobile 58,772) and none of them mean 'this shop comes to you'.

sources.name: OSMF Licence Community Guideline — Geocoding
sources.why_it_matters: This is the legal ruling that governs the whole design. Verbatim: individual geocoding results 'contain an insubstantial amount of raw OSM data' and 'may be stored and used together with other proprietary or third party data without having a share-alike impact' — BUT only where 'the Geocoding Results are not used to create a new database that contains the whole or a substantial part of the original OSM database', and substantiality is defined as 'a systematic attempt to aggregate all or substantially all Primary Features of a given type ... within a geographic area city-sized or larger'. Enriching every truck repair shop along every US truck route IS that systematic attempt. Therefore the narrow geocoding carve-out does NOT rescue copying OSM service tags into core.businesses.
sources.caveats: A community guideline, not a court ruling — it expresses OSMF's interpretation. It is nonetheless the standard the OSM community holds projects to, and the conservative reading is the safe one here.

sources.name: OSMF Licence Community Guideline — Horizontal Map Layers
sources.http_status: unknown — I located this via search and read the summary, I did not fetch the page body myself
sources.why_it_matters: The positive counterpart to the geocoding ruling and the legal foundation of the repo's existing section 3.1-4a: if all data for a Feature Type comes from non-OSM sources, ODbL share-alike does not apply to that Feature Type even when OSM data is used for other Feature Types. That is precisely why core.businesses (Overture + FSQ only, with the present_in CHECK forbidding 'osm') stays permissively licensed while osm.* sits alongside it. It also means the moment an OSM-derived 'services offered' value lands in core.businesses, that feature type flips to share-alike.
sources.caveats: [UNVERIFIED] — I did not fetch this page body directly; the wording above is from the search-result summary plus the OSMF Collective Database Guideline. Read the primary text before citing it in the repo's DECISION_LOG.

sources.name: opening-hours-py (PyPI) — OSM opening_hours parser
sources.why_it_matters: This is the 2026 answer to the task's 'opening_hours.js? python oh? something newer?' question. It is actively maintained (release 16 days ago), permissively dual-licensed MIT/Apache-2.0, and needs no Node runtime — which matters because the repo is a pure-Python + DuckDB + Postgres stack. Use it to derive open_24x7 and to validate any hours string before storing it.
sources.caveats: The canonical reference implementation remains opening_hours.js (npm, v3.14.0 published 2026-07-15) which is LGPL-3.0-only and claims to parse 99.3% of OSM opening_hours values; opening-hours-py's coverage against that benchmark is unmeasured by me. The old pyopening_hours is DEAD (0.3.0, last upload 2015-10-09, GPLv3) — do not use it. osm-opening-hours-humanized exists at 1.0.0b7 (2025-02-20) but is beta.

sources.name: extruct (PyPI) — schema.org / JSON-LD / microdata extractor
sources.why_it_matters: Still the standard one-call extractor for all structured-data flavours at once, which matters because 20% of the reachable shop sites I probed used microdata itemtype rather than JSON-LD. Pair with selectolax 0.4.11 (MIT, 2026-07-15) for fast HTML parsing, trafilatura 2.1.0 (Apache-2.0, 2026-06-07) for text fallback, and protego 0.6.2 (BSD-3, 2026-06-25) for robots.txt — protego is the maintained choice, reppy is dead (0.4.14, 2019).
sources.caveats: extruct's last release is 2024-11-08, so it is aging relative to the rest of the 2026 stack; no successor has displaced it. rdflib 7.6.0 and pyld 3.1.0 are current if full JSON-LD expansion is needed, but for LocalBusiness scraping a plain regex-plus-json.loads over <script type="application/ld+json"> is what I used and it was sufficient.

sources.name: Name Suggestion Index (NSI) — brand/chain normalisation
sources.approx_rows: 49,943 brand items across 408 category paths; brands/shop/car_repair 251, brands/shop/tyres 51, brands/shop/truck 20, brands/shop/truck_repair 17, brands/shop/car_parts 61, brands/amenity/fuel 711
sources.why_it_matters: The free, legal way to normalise the messy brand strings Overture and FSQ emit ('Ryder System, Inc.' vs 'Ryder', 'TravelCenters-TA-Petro') into a single canonical brand + a Wikidata QID. That QID is then the join key for chain-level facts. Repo already references NSI in the core.businesses DDL comment for the brand column, so this is a wiring task not a new dependency. Upstream repo is active (pushed 2026-07-23, 866 stars).
sources.caveats: The dist/*.json artifacts are NOT in the git repo main tree — they are build outputs published to npm and served via jsDelivr, so a build-pinned URL (as above) is required; raw.githubusercontent.com paths 404. NSI's truck_repair coverage is only 17 brands and is heavily non-US (Ashok Leyland, BharatBenz, DAF, Eicher, Fuso, Iveco appear first), so it will normalise US OEM dealer groups poorly.

sources.name: Wikidata Query Service (SPARQL)
sources.approx_rows: unknown for truck chains specifically; my probe returned 317 for one US chain-store class query
sources.why_it_matters: CC0 — the most permissive licence in this entire report. Joined via NSI's brand:wikidata QID it gives chain/parent-company facts (e.g. Speedco → Love's) for free, forever, with no attribution obligation. Useful for 'Truck Brands Supported' at the CHAIN level and for de-duplicating rebranded networks.
sources.caveats: Wikidata has essentially nothing at the individual-shop level — no hours, no phone, no services for a given location. It is a brand-level lookup only. Rate-limit and set a descriptive User-Agent; WDQS enforces both.

sources.name: NY DMV — Facilities Licensed by the Department of Motor Vehicles
sources.license: NY State open data terms; no licence string published in the dataset metadata (license field is empty), attribution 'NYS DMV'
sources.approx_rows: 54,563 total. Business types: RS (repair shop) 18,272 · DLU 10,815 · ISP (inspection station) 10,405 · RSB (repair shop, body) 3,426 · ATV 3,117 · TRS 1,746 · DLW 1,463 · DLN 1,340 · DLB 905 · DIS 551 · ABK 503. Of the 18,272 RS rows, 17,738 (97.1%) carry a georeference point.
sources.why_it_matters: This is the ONLY class of source that can honestly fill 'Verification Status' and 'Last Verified Date' — a live government licence with an expiry date is verification in a way that a POI record never is. It also fills County (the correct US mapping of the task's 'District') natively. Dataset is current: rowsUpdatedAt 2026-07-06, max RS expiration 2027-12-31, max last_renewal 2026-07-03. Keyless SODA API supports $select/$where/$group so you can pull only active licences.
sources.caveats: NY ONLY — there is no national equivalent, and my search of the federal and state open-data catalogues found no other state with comparable coverage. Carries NO phone, NO website, NO hours, NO services. The publisher's own disclaimer states 'Facilities expired less than 6 years are included in the data set', so you MUST filter on expiration_date or you will serve dead shops as verified. expiration_date is a TEXT column in MM/DD/YYYY format — string comparison against ISO dates silently returns zero rows (I hit this myself). Business-type codes are undocumented in the dataset; RS/RSB are inferable but TRS is not, and guessing would violate the honesty rules.

sources.name: NJ — Vehicle Inspection Facility Locations
sources.license: No licence string published in dataset metadata (license: null)
sources.why_it_matters: Unlike the NY dataset this one INCLUDES phone_no, plus county and a geocoded point — a government-sourced phone number is higher-trust than a crowd-sourced one and is a good conflation tie-breaker. Also carries a licence id and an inspection_type that reads as a coarse service category ('Emission Repair Only').
sources.caveats: Tiny (1,167 rows) and scoped to emissions-inspection/repair facilities, not truck repair — a class-8 diesel shop will mostly not appear. Data quality is visibly rough in the rows I pulled: one record has adr_street 'P.O.BOX 317' with city 'WATERFORD WORK' but county 'MORRIS' (Waterford Works is in Camden County), so county and address disagree. No licence is declared on the dataset, which is itself a compliance gap to resolve before republishing.

sources.name: US Census TIGER/Line — County boundaries (for the 'District' → County mapping)
sources.license: US Government work — public domain (no copyright)
sources.approx_rows: unknown (not enumerated — ~3,144 counties expected but I did not open the file)
sources.why_it_matters: The requested 'District' field has no US analogue; the correct mapping is County. TIGER is public domain, national, and PostGIS-loadable, so a single point-in-polygon join fills County for every shop at zero cost and zero licence risk. TIGER ZCTA520 (tl_2024_us_zcta520.zip, also verified 206) is available for the ZIP-ish geography.
sources.caveats: ZCTA is NOT the same as a USPS ZIP Code — do not use ZCTA to populate a field labelled ZIP. For the actual ZIP, use the postcode already present in Overture addresses[] / FSQ postcode. TIGER county boundaries change between vintages, so pin the year and record it in lineage.

sources.name: FCC Census Block Conversions API (keyless point → county)
sources.http_status: 206 (JSON body returned: county_fips 36119, county_name 'Westchester County', state_code NY)
sources.why_it_matters: A zero-setup alternative to loading TIGER when you only need county for a handful of points — no key, no download, returns county name and FIPS directly from lat/lon. Useful for spot-checks and for the 'District → County' mapping during development.
sources.caveats: Per-request HTTP call, so unusable for 200k+ shops at national scale — use TIGER + PostGIS ST_Contains for the bulk job and keep this for verification. Rate limits are undocumented; must go through the repo's polite_get() choke point like everything else.

sources.name: Love's Travel Stops — locations sitemap + Terms of Use
fields_provided: location page URLs (name, city, state inferable from slug)
sources.why_it_matters: Answers the task's Love's/Speedco question definitively and negatively. Despite an allow-all robots.txt and a published locations sitemap, the Terms of Use say, verbatim: 'Without the prior written consent of Love's, you are not allowed (i) to modify, copy, mine, scrape, distribute, transmit, display, perform, reproduce, publish, license, create derivative works from, transfer or sell any information or material, products or services obtained from the Online Properties'. That is an explicit, unambiguous prohibition on scraping AND on reproducing the data. UNUSABLE. Speedco is now part of Love's Truck Care and speedco.com does not resolve, so it falls under the same prohibition.
sources.caveats: robots.txt being permissive is NOT permission — this is the clearest example in the whole lane of why robots.txt and ToS must both be checked. Love's locations remain reachable legally through Overture's brand field instead.

The ToS overrides all of it. Note also the JSON-LD carries NO openingHours, so even if it were permitted it would not solve the hours field.

sources.name: Shop-own-website JSON-LD prevalence — my own measurement (n=120 US/PA auto repair shops)
sources.license: n/a (measurement, not a dataset); sample drawn from FSQ OS Places Apache-2.0
sources.why_it_matters: This is the empirical answer to 'how common is JSON-LD on small US repair-shop sites, realistically?' — and it is much worse than the schema.org marketing suggests. Of 120 FSQ-listed shops with a website: robots.txt returned 200 for 50, 404 for 13, and connection-errored for 46; ZERO sites disallowed the fetch. Only 51 (42%) served HTTP 200 — 47 (39%) were dead at the connection layer, 11 returned 403 (bot blocks), 11 returned other non-200. Of the 51 reachable: 24 (47%) had ANY JSON-LD block, but only 8 (16%) exposed telephone, 9 (18%) address, 6 (12%) openingHours, 7 (14%) geo, 2 (4%) email, 1 (2%) aggregateRating, 11 (22%) sameAs, and ZERO (0%) exposed makesOffer / hasOfferCatalog / serviceType. Type frequency: WebSite 17, WebPage 10, BreadcrumbList 8, Organization 8, ImageObject 6, Article 3, Person 3, AutoDealer 3, LocalBusiness 2, AutomotiveBusiness 2, AutoRepair 1, AutoPartsStore 1. Only ONE site in 51 used the AutoRepair type. Plain-HTML heuristics beat JSON-LD: tel: links on 24 (47%), mailto: links on 7 (14%). CONCLUSION: 'Services Offered' is NEVER available from JSON-LD on small shop sites, and end-to-end hours yield from website extraction is roughly 0.63 (has website in FSQ) x 0.42 (reachable) x 0.12 (has openingHours) ≈ 3% of shops.
sources.caveats: Sample is Pennsylvania-only (all 120 rows came from one FSQ shard) and the URLs come from the FROZEN 2025-02-06 mirror, so the 39% dead rate conflates genuine business closure with 18 months of URL rot — the true dead rate against the current HF release will be lower. n=51 reachable is small, so each percentage carries roughly ±7pp. The 11 x 403 responses mean some sites actively block bots even without a robots.txt rule, and those must be recorded as skips, never retried harder.

recommendations: FIRST, HIGHEST ROI, ZERO NEW SOURCES: add `emails` and `socials` to _OVERTURE_STAGING_COLS in /home/ujjwal/Documents/truck-intel/scripts/businesses_pipeline.py and add email TEXT + socials TEXT[] columns to core.businesses. I measured 60.4% email fill and 82.1% socials fill on Overture's 10,924 CONUS truck_repair rows — the pipeline is currently discarding roughly 6,600 truck-repair email addresses and ~9,000 social handles on every single pull. This is a projection bug, not a data-availability problem, and it is the cheapest win in the whole lane.

TURN ON THE FSQ PULL AND USE IT PRIMARILY FOR EMAIL. FSQ OS Places is the only free legal BULK email source in existence for this domain (Apache-2.0, `email` is a first-class column). I measured 41.0% email fill on 57,753 US 'Automotive Repair Shop' rows. Mint a free Hugging Face token for the current release (dt=2026-07-09) rather than staying on the frozen source.coop mirror — but tell Boss first that the HF gate requires consenting to Foursquare using his entity name/logo in marketing material. Merge rule: Overture is canonical for email where both have it (higher fill, fresher release), FSQ fills NULLs.

DERIVE THE SERVICE FLAGS FROM OVERTURE'S CATEGORY TAXONOMY, NOT FROM SCRAPING. Overture already ships roadside_assistance, emergency_roadside_service, mobile_dent_repair, trailer_repair, truck_repair, truck_repair_and_services_for_businesses and welders as categories (verified in the live overture_categories.csv). Map these to the requested Towing / Roadside Breakdown / Mobile Service / Welding / Tyre Repair booleans. This is licence-clean, national, and needs no new fetching. Be honest in the render: a category tells you what the business IS, not the full set of what it OFFERS, so every unset flag must render as "unknown", never "no".

DO NOT COPY ANY OSM ATTRIBUTE INTO core.businesses — the existing ruling section 3.1-4a is legally correct and this task is precisely the case it guards against. The OSMF Geocoding Guideline defines substantiality as 'a systematic attempt to aggregate all or substantially all Primary Features of a given type within a geographic area city-sized or larger', which is exactly national truck-repair enrichment. Keep opening_hours and service:vehicle:* in osm.*, join at query time, and expose them through the API as a separately-labelled, ODbL-attributed layer (e.g. an `osm_corroboration` sub-object) so the Horizontal Map Layers feature-type independence holds.

BUILD THE HOURS FIELD ON OSM opening_hours ONLY, AND SET EXPECTATIONS AT ~15% NATIONAL COVERAGE. It is the only free structured hours source that exists — Overture has no hours field (confirmed on the live schema doc), FSQ has none, and website JSON-LD yields hours for only ~3% of shops end-to-end. Parse with opening-hours-py 2.1.4 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, released 2026-07-07, Rust-backed, no Node needed) rather than the LGPL opening_hours.js or the dead pyopening_hours. Derive open_24x7 by exact string match on '24/7' first (it is 15.7% of all opening_hours values globally) and only fall back to the parser for complex expressions.

ADD STATE LICENCE REGISTRIES AS THE 'VERIFICATION STATUS' AND 'LAST VERIFIED DATE' SOURCE, STARTING WITH NY. data.ny.gov/d/nhjr-rpi2 gives 18,272 licensed repair shops (RS) plus 3,426 body shops (RSB), 97.1% of them geocoded, refreshed 2026-07-06, keyless SODA API, with expiration_date. A live government licence is the only defensible basis for a 'verified' badge. TWO TRAPS I HIT: expiration_date is TEXT in MM/DD/YYYY so ISO string comparison silently returns zero rows, and the publisher includes facilities expired up to 6 years — you must filter or you will publish dead shops as verified. NJ (data.nj.gov/d/t6tk-mr48, 1,167 rows) additionally carries phone_no. Treat this as per-state and patchy; there is no national registry.

SET THE PER-FIELD FILL-RATE BUDGET HONESTLY IN THE SPEC BEFORE BUILDING. My measured expectations for a US truck-repair shop, using Overture as base + FSQ as filler: name 100%, lat/lon 100%, address ~98%, state ~98%, ZIP ~98%, county ~100% (derived via TIGER PIP), phone 95-99%, website 67-70%, EMAIL 50-60%, socials ~82%, brand/chain 5-15% (but ~90%+ for the chains that matter), services-offered-as-category ~100% coarse / 0% fine-grained, open_24x7 ~10-15% (OSM-joined, and only where an OSM match exists at all), operating hours ~15% (same), towing/roadside/mobile/welding flags 100% coarse from category, tyre/battery/spare-parts ~0-1% fine-grained, TRUCK BRANDS SUPPORTED ~5% (Overture brand on truck_repair) rising toward ~15-20% if the OEM dealer networks are ever legally unlocked. Ship these numbers in the README so nobody later mistakes a sparse column for a broken pipeline.

WEBSITE FETCHING IS WORTH DOING BUT BUDGET IT AS A ~20% PHONE / ~6% EMAIL / ~3% HOURS TOP-UP, NOT AS THE ENRICHMENT ENGINE. My n=120 probe says: extract tel: hrefs and mailto: links (47% and 14% of reachable pages) BEFORE trying JSON-LD (16% telephone, 4% email) — the plain-HTML heuristic beats the structured one on small shop sites. Use extruct 0.18.0 to catch microdata too (20% of reachable sites used itemtype rather than JSON-LD), protego 0.6.2 for robots.txt (reppy is dead since 2019), selectolax 0.4.11 for parsing. Route every request through the existing polite_get() choke point, record 403s and connection errors as ops.source_runs skips rather than retrying harder, and never re-fetch a host that 403s.

TREAT LOVE'S, RYDER AND TA/PETRO AS PERMANENTLY OFF LIMITS AND WRITE THAT DOWN IN THE REPO. All three have explicit anti-scraping clauses I quoted verbatim from their live Terms of Use today, and all three have permissive robots.txt and published location sitemaps that will tempt a future contributor. Add them to a data/config/forbidden_sources.yaml with the verbatim clause and the evidence URL so the decision does not have to be re-litigated. Their locations are reachable legally through Overture's brand field anyway (TravelCenters-TA-Petro 104 rows, Ryder 431, Pilot 19).

BEFORE ANY OEM DEALER FETCH, HAVE A HUMAN READ THE ACTUAL ToS FOR FREIGHTLINER, PETERBILT, MACK, VOLVO TRUCKS NA, WESTERN STAR AND INTERNATIONAL. I verified their robots.txt are allow-all and that Freightliner's dealer pages carry schema.org LocalBusiness JSON-LD with telephone — but I could NOT retrieve any of their terms-of-use text (SPA-rendered or 404). Given that every large chain ToS I could read prohibits scraping, the honest default is unusable. Kenworth returns 403 on robots.txt and should be treated as an active refusal. In the meantime, ship 'Truck Brands Supported' from Overture's brand field + Name Suggestion Index (BSD-3-Clause, jsDelivr-pinned) + Wikidata QID (CC0) — that path is already legal today and already resolves MHC Kenworth, TLG Peterbilt, Premier Truck Group, Velocity Truck Centers, Vanguard, TEC Equipment, Rush Truck Centers, TruckPro and FleetPride.

RENAME THE INDIA-VOCABULARY FIELDS IN THE SPEC NOW, BEFORE ANY CODE IS WRITTEN: 'District' -> 'county' (+ county_fips), filled by point-in-polygon against Census TIGER tl_2024_us_county.zip (public domain, verified live) or the keyless FCC Census Block API for spot-checks; 'PIN Code' -> 'zip' (5-digit USPS, already present in Overture addresses[].postcode and FSQ postcode) — and do NOT substitute Census ZCTA for ZIP, they are different geographies; 'WhatsApp Number' -> DELETE the field entirely (see unfillable). Leaving India vocabulary in a US-only schema will confuse every future reader and will eventually produce a wrong join.

DROP average_rating, review_count, review_summary, photos AND whatsapp FROM THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN SHIPPING FIVE PERPETUALLY-NULL COLUMNS. Neither Overture nor FSQ carries any of them (I confirmed the absence on both live schema docs), and every source that does — Google, Yelp, TripAdvisor — prohibits programmatic extraction. A column that is 100% NULL forever is worse than no column: it invites a future contributor to 'fix' it by scraping. If a review signal is genuinely needed later, the only honest free proxy is the government licence status from the state registries plus Overture's own per-record confidence score, and it should be named something like trust_score, never 'rating'.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Average Rating / Review Count / Review Summary
unfillable_or_risky.problem: No free legal US source exists, full stop. Overture's places schema has no rating or review field (confirmed on the live schema doc today). FSQ OS Places has no rating or review count (confirmed on the live schema doc). OSM does not carry ratings. Every source that does have them — Google Places, Yelp Fusion, TripAdvisor — is either paid, prohibits storage/redistribution in its ToS, or both. My own website probe found aggregateRating on exactly 1 of 51 reachable shop sites (2%), and even that single instance would be a per-site scrape of unverifiable self-reported data.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: There is no substitute and Boss should be told that plainly. The closest honest signals, which must NOT be labelled 'rating': (a) Overture's per-record `confidence` score, which I measured at 0.839 average for truck_repair and 0.814 for automotive_repair — a data-quality score, not a customer-satisfaction score; (b) government licence status + expiration date from state registries such as data.ny.gov/d/nhjr-rpi2, which is a real trust signal ('currently licensed by NY DMV, expires 2027-03-31'); (c) present_in cardinality (a shop confirmed by both Overture and FSQ is more likely real). Expose these as trust_score / license_status and never as a star rating.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: No free legal source at meaningful coverage. Overture and FSQ carry no image fields. Google/Yelp images are ToS-prohibited and copyright-encumbered. Wikimedia Commons has essentially zero coverage of individual US truck repair shops. Mapillary is street-level imagery (not shop photos), is CC-BY-SA (share-alike, which would infect a produced work), and its API requires a token.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Omit the field. If a visual is genuinely required for UX, render a map tile or a category icon rather than claiming a photo of the premises. Do not hotlink images from shop websites — that is both a copyright issue and a bandwidth-theft issue.

unfillable_or_risky.problem: This is an India-vocabulary field with no US analogue. WhatsApp is not the default business-contact channel for US truck repair shops, and there is no dataset — free, paid, or otherwise — that flags a US business phone as WhatsApp-enabled. FSQ carries facebook_id / instagram / twitter but nothing WhatsApp. Overture's `socials` array is URL-based; I sampled the domain mix on truck_repair but the run was cut short, so I cannot state what fraction (if any) are wa.me links. Probing numbers against WhatsApp to test enrolment would be an unauthorised automated query against a third-party service.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Delete the field. Replace it with the legally available social handles: Overture `socials` (82.1% fill on truck_repair — currently discarded by the pipeline) and FSQ facebook_id (14.6% of US rows) / instagram (0.7%). If a messaging channel is genuinely wanted, a tel: link plus an SMS deep-link is the honest US equivalent and needs no new data.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Services Offered (fine-grained: welding, spare parts, tyre repair, battery service, DPF, alignment) as a per-shop verified list
unfillable_or_risky.problem: There is no source at national scale. OSM's service:vehicle:* family is the only structured vocabulary and it is empirically tiny in the US: over a CONUS bbox I measured shop=car_repair with service:vehicle:truck_repair at 448 rows out of 52,713 (0.85%), and shop=truck_repair at 330 rows nationally. Globally service:vehicle:truck_repair is 1,381 uses and service:vehicle:towing is 772. Worse, even those values cannot be copied into core.businesses without dragging the field under ODbL share-alike. Shop websites do not help: ZERO of the 51 reachable sites I probed exposed makesOffer, hasOfferCatalog or serviceType in JSON-LD. Free-text scraping of service menus would be an unlicensed derivative of each shop's copyrighted page content.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Two-tier honesty. TIER 1 (ship this): coarse service flags derived from Overture's own category taxonomy — roadside_assistance, emergency_roadside_service, mobile_dent_repair, trailer_repair, truck_repair, welders, tire_dealer_and_repair, towing_service all exist as categories, are CDLA-Permissive, and cover 100% of rows. TIER 2 (query-time only): OSM service:vehicle:* surfaced as a separate ODbL-attributed corroboration object joined at read time, never merged into core.businesses, and honestly labelled as covering under 1% of shops. Every unset flag renders as "unknown", never "no".

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Mobile Service / Roadside Breakdown as a per-shop capability flag
unfillable_or_risky.problem: No structured tag or field exists anywhere for 'this shop will come to your truck'. I enumerated every OSM key containing 'mobile' via taginfo and the top results are communication:mobile_phone (256,973), snowmobile (118,675), mobile (70,749), contact:mobile (58,772) — none of them mean mobile mechanic service. There is no equivalent in FSQ. Inferring it from a shop's name ('XYZ Mobile Truck Repair') is a heuristic, and the repo's section 6 DEF ruling makes clear that brand-based DEF inference is the ONLY permitted inference in the entire platform, so a name-based mobile-service inference would violate a binding architectural rule.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Use Overture's dedicated categories as the ONLY basis: roadside_assistance, emergency_roadside_service and mobile_dent_repair are first-class Overture category slugs. A place whose primary category IS roadside_assistance can honestly be flagged mobile=true. A truck_repair shop that also happens to offer mobile service is NOT discoverable from any free source and must stay NULL/unknown. Do not extend the DEF-style inference exemption to cover this without an explicit new ruling from Boss.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Truck Brands Supported (Freightliner / Peterbilt / Kenworth / Mack / Volvo / International / Western Star authorisation per shop)
unfillable_or_risky.problem: The authoritative sources are the OEM dealer locators, and their legal status is either explicitly prohibited or unverified. Of the chains whose Terms of Use I could actually read, ALL THREE prohibit automated access: Love's ('modify, copy, mine, scrape...'), Ryder ('any robot, spider, scraper, deep link or other similar automated data gathering'), TA/Petro ('Use any robot, spider or other automatic device'). For the truck OEMs I could not retrieve the ToS text at all — Freightliner /legal/terms-of-use/ 404s and its footer links only to a Daimler privacy policy; Peterbilt /terms is an unrendered SPA; Mack and Volvo /legal/terms-of-use/ 404; International serves no robots.txt; Kenworth returns 403 even on robots.txt. Marking these 'permitted' because robots.txt is blank would be exactly the reasoning error that TA/Petro and Love's disprove.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Ship a partial, honest version today from Overture's `brand` field, which is CDLA-Permissive and needs no fetching at all. On truck-ish CONUS categories it already resolves Penske 1553, Budget 376, Ryder System Inc 357, U-Haul 180, Enterprise 110, Rush Truck Centers 107, TravelCenters-TA-Petro 104, Ryder 74, MHC Kenworth 62, Boss Truck Shop 43, FleetPride/GSFA 38, Premier Truck Group 25, Velocity Truck Centers 23, TLG Peterbilt 22, Vanguard Truck Centers 21, W W Williams 20, TEC Equipment 16, TruckPro 14. Normalise those strings with the Name Suggestion Index (BSD-3-Clause, 49,943 items, pinned via jsDelivr) and join to Wikidata QIDs (CC0) for parent-company rollup. Expected coverage is only ~5% of truck_repair rows, but it is 100% legal and it covers the chains that actually matter. Label the field brand_network, and render NULL as "unknown", so nobody reads a NULL as 'this shop does not service Peterbilts'.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Operating Hours and Open 24x7 at usable national coverage
unfillable_or_risky.problem: Overture has NO hours field at all — the live schema doc explicitly states operating_status is 'not an indication of opening hours'. FSQ has no hours column. That leaves only OSM opening_hours, which is ODbL share-alike AND sparse: over a CONUS bbox I measured 8,165 of 52,713 shop=car_repair rows carrying opening_hours (15.5%), and shop=truck_repair is only 330 rows nationally. Website extraction does not rescue it: only 12% of the 51 reachable shop sites I probed exposed openingHours in JSON-LD, and only 42% of sites were reachable at all, giving roughly 3% end-to-end yield. For a driver broken down at 2am, a field that is 85%+ unknown is close to useless.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Serve OSM opening_hours as a query-time join from osm.* with explicit ODbL attribution and an honest coverage disclaimer, parsed with opening-hours-py 2.1.4 (MIT OR Apache-2.0). Derive open_24x7 by exact match on the literal '24/7' value first — it accounts for 738,170 uses, 15.7% of all opening_hours values globally, so most of the 24/7 signal needs no parser. Render every shop without an OSM hours match as "unknown", never as closed and never as 'call to confirm' phrased as if it were data. Consider surfacing 'phone: 99.2% available' as the actionable fallback, since the phone number IS almost always there.

unfillable_or_risky.field_or_claim: Nearest Highway Junction / Travel Direction / Nearest Route Point / Distance from Route / Route ID / Route Name
unfillable_or_risky.problem: Out of scope for this lane and, more importantly, blocked upstream: the orchestrator's ground truth confirms THERE IS NO ROUTES TABLE anywhere in sql/schema.sql, sql/schema_wave2.sql or sql/schema_phase2.sql, and no route_id/route_name concept exists. Every one of these six fields is a function of a route geometry that does not yet exist in the database. Additionally the US OSM backfill is not running and osm.ways covers only a Delaware bbox (lon -75.85..-75.05, lat 38.40..39.87), so even the road geometry needed to compute a junction is absent for 99% of the country.
unfillable_or_risky.best_legal_alternative: Do not attempt these fields until a routes table exists and the national OSM ways backfill has completed. When it does, the legal ingredients are all free: OSM highway ways (ODbL, query-time only) for junctions and route geometry, plus PostGIS ST_Distance / ST_LineLocatePoint for distance-from-route and nearest-route-point. Travel direction is derivable from the route linestring's bearing at the nearest point. Note the same ODbL constraint applies — a computed distance-to-an-OSM-way stored in core.businesses is an OSM-derived value, so these should live in a derived osm-lineage table or be computed at request time.

open_questions: Does Overture's `socials` array actually contain any wa.me / WhatsApp URLs for US truck_repair, or is it purely Facebook/Instagram/X? My domain-mix query on socials for truck_repair was killed before it returned, so I only know the fill rate (82.1%) and not the composition. One cheap DuckDB query over the CONUS bbox settles whether 'WhatsApp Number' has ANY legal path at all, or whether it should be deleted outright as I have recommended.

What is the true OSM phone fill rate for shop=car_repair in the US? My combined phone/contact:phone Overpass query returned 0 because of my own regex-escaping error in the query string, so this number is UNMEASURED. Global taginfo suggests 19.6% phone + 3.9% contact:phone, but US is consistently worse than global for OSM POI attributes. Two simple separate Overpass count queries would fix this.

Does the current FSQ Hugging Face release (dt=2026-07-09) have materially better email fill and materially fewer dead website URLs than the frozen 2025-02-06 source.coop mirror I measured? My 39% dead-URL rate conflates real closures with 18 months of link rot. Worth re-running the 120-site probe against the current release before setting the website-extraction budget.

Is my Overture fill-rate measurement stable under an empty-array check? I verified on one 4,595,262-row shard that Overture stores NULL and never an empty array for phones/emails/websites (0 empty arrays observed), which validates count(col). But my confirming national re-run with explicit len(col)>0 logic was still scanning when I finished and did not return. The numbers are almost certainly correct; a single re-run would remove the last doubt.

What do Peterbilt, Mack, Volvo Trucks NA, Western Star and International actually say in their Terms of Use? All five serve permissive or absent robots.txt, and Freightliner's dealer pages carry usable schema.org LocalBusiness JSON-LD — but I could not render any of their ToS pages. This is the single highest-value unresolved legal question in the lane, because it is the difference between ~5% and ~20% coverage on 'Truck Brands Supported'. It needs a human to open five pages and read them.

Beyond NY and NJ, which other states publish a free bulk repair-facility or towing licence registry? My Socrata catalogue search surfaced only NY (54,563 rows), NJ (1,167), CT (138 rows and mostly manufacturers — useless), Montgomery County MD 'Motor Vehicle Repair and Towing', and NYC 'DARP-ROTOW Active Tow Truck Companies'. California explicitly charges for bulk BAR licensee lists, so CA is not free. A systematic 50-state sweep would establish whether the 'verified' badge can reach beyond the Northeast.

Does Overture publish per-record source provenance granular enough to satisfy the repo's honesty rule that observed_at is when the fact was true in the world? Overture's `sources[]` array exists in the schema but I did not inspect its contents. If it carries a per-source update date, observed_at could be materially more accurate than the current 'release date' approximation, especially for phone and email which may be years older than the release.

Should the 'services offered' concept be modelled as a single primary category (matching Overture's model, 100% coverage but coarse) or as an array of capability flags (matching the request, but under 1% coverage and ODbL-encumbered)? This is a schema decision with a licensing consequence and it should be Boss's call, not mine — the two options give very different products and I do not want to pre-narrow it.
